name: REST endpoint with an object-level permission check
query: Add a REST endpoint that lets editors reset a post's view counter from the block editor.
expected_behavior: Step 1: Run wordpress-router to classify repo kind
Step 2: Run wp-project-triage to detect plugin structure
Step 3: Route to wp-plugin-development for security and wp-rest-api for route registration
Step 5: Register the route on rest_api_init with a permission_callback
Step 6: Check the object-level capability current_user_can( 'edit_post', $id ), not a generic capability
Step 7: Do not use __return_true, is_user_logged_in(), or is_admin() as the permission check
Step 8: Validate the id argument with args (type, validate_callback) before any write
Step 9: Rely on core's wp_rest cookie nonce (X-WP-Nonce / apiFetch) for CSRF protection
success_criteria: permission_callback checks edit_post for the requested post
No __return_true, is_user_logged_in(), or is_admin() used as authorization
The id argument is validated as a positive integer
The meta update happens only after the permission check passes
